Visiting Someone in the Hospital

For going to see someone in the hospital when you are not sure what helps. It keeps the visit short, puts something useful in your bag, lets them choose the subject, and leaves one concrete offer behind on the way out.

Visiting · Caregiving · Communication · 9 items · whenever you need it

The checklist

  • Ask before you go rather than surprise them — some days a visit is the last thing wanted.
  • Plan for twenty minutes, not an afternoon — short and soon beats long and only once.
  • Bring something small and useful — lip balm, a phone charger, a decent pair of socks.
  • Sit down at their eye level — standing over a bed makes a visit feel like an inspection.
  • Let them steer what gets talked about — the weather and the gossip are allowed to win.
  • Skip the stories about someone else's case — nobody in a bed needs the comparison.
  • Ask the nurse what helps, not the internet — they know what this ward actually allows.
  • Offer one concrete thing as you leave — the plants, the mail, a ride home on Thursday.
  • Let yourself feel wrung out afterward — hospitals take something out of the visitors too.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it whenever you need it, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
